title: Brindle Isle
text: Brindle Isle is the northernmost island of the Aldervane Archipelago, known for its terraced kelp orchards. The Saltglass Lighthouse stands on its northern cliff, and the ferry Grey Heron calls at its small harbor twice a day.

title: Cobalt Isle
text: Cobalt Isle is the southern island of the archipelago. Its dunes supply the fine blue-white sand prized by glassmakers, and its hills hold shallow veins of copper. The island is best known as the home of the Ferro Foundry.

title: Saltglass Lighthouse
text: The Saltglass Lighthouse stands on the northern cliff of Brindle Isle. Since 1987 its keeper has been Mara Venn, who took over from her uncle Odo Venn. The lighthouse's green-glass lens was cast at the Ferro Foundry.

title: Mara Venn
text: Mara Venn is an inventor and the current keeper of the Saltglass Lighthouse. She is best known for inventing the tidewriter, a brass instrument that records tide heights on paper ribbons. She sells her tidewriters at the Windrow Market.

title: Odo Venn
text: Odo Venn kept the Saltglass Lighthouse for thirty years before retiring in 1987. After leaving lightkeeping he founded the Tidewatch Observatory on Fenn Rock, where he lived until his death.

title: Ferro Foundry
text: The Ferro Foundry on Cobalt Isle produces glasswork and bronze fittings for the whole archipelago. Its head artisan is Tobin Rask. In 1979 the foundry cast the green-glass lens of the Saltglass Lighthouse.

title: Tobin Rask
text: Tobin Rask is the head artisan of the Ferro Foundry, celebrated for his seaglass casting technique. He is the younger brother of Sela Rask and trains two apprentices every summer.

title: Sela Rask
text: Sela Rask runs the Saltmarsh Market on Merrow Isle. The older sister of Tobin Rask, she began her working life as a rope maker before taking over the market's barge fleet.

title: Windrow Market
text: The Windrow Market is held every week on Halewick Isle and is overseen by the harbormaster Liss Harrow. Its stalls are famous for brass instruments, dried kelp, and chart paper.

title: Saltmarsh Market
text: The Saltmarsh Market is the floating market of Merrow Isle, held on a fleet of flat-bottomed barges. It is run by Sela Rask and moves its moorings with the season.

title: Halewick Isle
text: Halewick Isle is the busiest island of the archipelago. It hosts the Windrow Market and the hall of the Cartographers' Guild, and its deep harbor is the eastern terminus of the ferry Grey Heron.

title: Grey Heron
text: The Grey Heron is the iron-hulled ferry that links Brindle Isle and Halewick Isle. She was built at the Kelvane Foundry and has been captained by Edda Quill for two decades.

title: Edda Quill
text: Edda Quill is the captain of the ferry Grey Heron. Born on Merrow Isle, she keeps the ferry's log in violet ink and is said to read the currents better than any chart.

title: Cartographers' Guild
text: The Cartographers' Guild keeps its hall on Halewick Isle and maintains the official charts of the archipelago. The guild is led by Bram Copperline, and it redraws the tide charts each spring.

title: Bram Copperline
text: Bram Copperline leads the Cartographers' Guild. He apprenticed under Ivo Marsh and engraved the first complete chart of Fenn Rock, a work that took him four years.

title: Tidewatch Observatory
text: The Tidewatch Observatory is perched on the granite dome of Fenn Rock. Odo Venn founded it after his retirement from lightkeeping, and its brass tide gauges are checked at every dawn.

title: Nyra Fenwick
text: Nyra Fenwick is the astronomer of the Tidewatch Observatory. She was the first to document the double tide of Merrow Isle, and she publishes the archipelago's Tide Almanac every year.

title: Fenn Rock
text: Fenn Rock is the smallest inhabited island of the archipelago, a bare granite dome with a single stair-stepped village. It is home to the Tidewatch Observatory, and the Mistral Bell hangs in its harbor tower.

title: Mistral Bell
text: The Mistral Bell is the bronze bell that hangs in the harbor tower of Fenn Rock. It was cast by Josper Hale, and it is rung only when the double tide is sighted.

title: Josper Hale
text: Josper Hale is the bellfounder of the Kelvane Foundry. He cast the Mistral Bell, and he learned his craft at the Ferro Foundry under Tobin Rask before returning to Ashvane Isle.

title: Kelvane Foundry
text: The Kelvane Foundry stands on Ashvane Isle and specializes in iron hulls and cast bells. It built the ferry Grey Heron, and it has been run by the Hale family for three generations.

title: Ashvane Isle
text: Ashvane Isle is the westernmost island, ringed by black-sand shores. It is home to the Kelvane Foundry, and each autumn it hosts the Lantern Festival that closes the storm season.

title: Lantern Festival
text: The Lantern Festival is held each autumn on Ashvane Isle to mark the close of the storm season. It was founded by Liss Harrow, and it ends with a flotilla of lantern-lit boats.

title: Liss Harrow
text: Liss Harrow is the harbormaster of Halewick Isle and the founder of the Lantern Festival. She sails a red-sailed sloop named the Petrel and signs every harbor ledger herself.

title: Merrow Isle
text: Merrow Isle is a low, marshy island famous for its double tide. It hosts the Saltmarsh Market, and at low water it is connected to Halewick Isle by a stone causeway.

title: Ivo Marsh
text: Ivo Marsh was the first magistrate of the Aldervane Archipelago and the author of the Deepwater Charter. Born on Merrow Isle, he spent his last years teaching chartmaking in the guild hall.

title: Deepwater Charter
text: The Deepwater Charter is the founding agreement of the Aldervane Archipelago, written by Ivo Marsh in 1901. It grants each island one vote in council, and the original is kept at the Cartographers' Guild.

title: Tidewriter
text: The tidewriter is a brass instrument that records tide heights on a moving paper ribbon. It was invented by Mara Venn, and every harbor in the archipelago keeps one, calibrated each year at the Tidewatch Observatory.

title: Double tide
text: The double tide is a rare second high tide seen only in the waters around Merrow Isle. Nyra Fenwick was the first to document it, timing its return from the Tidewatch Observatory.

title: Aldervane Archipelago
text: The Aldervane Archipelago is a chain of six inhabited islands: Brindle, Cobalt, Halewick, Merrow, Ashvane, and Fenn Rock. Island affairs are governed in council under the Deepwater Charter.
